text:
kelsey: Proposal ping: lightweight "hosting preference" surface to let clients say prefer/require/avoid + optional strict flag. aiming for minimal API churn. want quick design sanity check.

kelsey: Use cases: 1) tenant prefers Dedicated for lower p99; 2) tenant requires Private for compliance; 3) tenant asks to avoid hosted during sales trial.

martin: Quick note: we must avoid adding topology knowledge to clients. preference should be opaque (dedicated/private/hosted) not zone-level.

irene: billing question: if prefer->dedicated but resolves to hosted, how do we bill? recommend always bill by resolved routing, but surface a reconciliation log for billing.

yusuf: Implementation options I see: A) header-only approach: Prefer-Hosting + X-Hosting-Resolved returned B) token-based capability: control plane mints ephemeral hosting_grant tokens that encode guarantees C) manifest-level affordances where app declares required capabilities at deploy time.

kelsey: pros/cons noted: header-only is simplest for rollout. token gives stronger guarantees but increases auth surface. manifest-level helps operators but slower to change.

martin: For "require" semantics we need fail-fast behavior. Suggest mapping -> HTTP 424 with body {"error":"hosting_unavailable","requested":"private","reason":"no-capacity"}. For avoid we should never fall back to avoided mode; return 412 if unavoidable? maybe 409.

irene: Compliance wants an immutable audit entry: requested mode, resolved mode, decision timestamp, operator id if manual override. Add a structured log line even if header-only.

yusuf: Observability: emit metric hosting.requested.{mode} and hosting.resolved.{mode}, and a latency bucket when preference added. Also trace a tag hosting.pref_hit=true/false.

billing-bot: FYI: If billing by resolved routing, need reconciliation export at least once/day and per-tenant breakdown. Raising this as required for GA.

ops-bot: linked draft rfc: rfc-hosting-pref (WIP). note: add feature flag to gate token issuance.

kelsey: edge-case: what about burst capacity? if tenant prefers dedicated but dedicated is saturated transiently and hosted is available, is it OK to route to hosted for short periods? I think yes for prefer but not for require. need SLA around "preferred" fallbacks windows to avoid flapping.

martin: Agree on hysteresis. runtime should prefer sticky routing if the tenant recently hit dedicated; otherwise backoff attempts to avoid jittering.

irene: Another edge-case: per-request preference vs per-deployment preference. Some clients want per-request (ad-hoc), others want manifest-level (always). Support both but clarify precedence.

yusuf: Security: if we add hosting_grant tokens, they must be scoped and short-lived. Do not allow tokens to be reused across tenants. Also ensure tokens don't leak capacity info in plaintext.

kelsey: rollout plan suggestion: step1 header-only prefer/require/avoid + telemetry + logs step2 add X-Hosting-Resolved header and standard error payloads step3 optional hosted_grant token behind feature flag and opt-in tenants step4 manifest affordances RFC for advanced capabilities.

martin: Implementation detail: define canonical values: prefer|require|avoid and strict=true|false. parse tolerant: allow synonyms but normalize in logs.

irene: For billing compliance add a reconciliation API that returns rows: timestamp, tenant, requested, resolved, cost_center_tag. billing-bot: can follow up with required schema.

yusuf: One more: vendor-specific capabilities (eg int8-only) must not be exposed unless tenant opts into feature gates in manifest. avoid advertising runtime capabilities automatically.

kelsey: Action: I'll draft RFC with sample request/response, error codes, metric names, log format, and rollout plan. tagging @martin @irene @yusuf for review. would like sign-off on error codes and billing plan before prototyping.

ops-bot: reminder: link RFC in #architecture when ready and add telemetry checklist to the RFC.
